summary: Give the Wheel horsepower calculator the engine horsepower, the gearbox efficiency and the bearing efficiency and it returns rear wheel drivetrain efficiency. It is built for a practical question that turns up in daily life. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Wheel horsepower calculator work?
sections.html:
The Wheel horsepower calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports rear wheel drivetrain efficiency in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the drive type); then you type in the engine horsepower, the gearbox efficiency (Gearbox), the gearbox efficiency (Gearbox) and the bearing efficiency (Gearbox parameters).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Wheel horsepower calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Rear wheel drivetrain efficiency=wheel horsepower ÷ engine horsepower
Rear wheel drivetrain efficiency=differential efficiency × driveshaft efficiency × gearbox efficiency × propeller shaft efficiency
Number of gear meshes=the natural log of ((bearing efficiency ^ -number of bearings) × gearbox efficiency) ÷ the natural log of (gear mesh efficiency)
Bearing efficiency=((universal joint efficiency ^ -number of universal joints) × propeller shaft efficiency, 1 ÷ number of bearings)
Bearing efficiency=(differential efficiency × (gear mesh efficiency ^ -number of gear meshes), 1 ÷ number of bearings)
Driveshaft efficiency=rzeppa joint efficiency × tripod joint efficiency

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Drive type set to Rear wheel drive (RWD), Engine horsepower = 10 hp(l) and Wheel horsepower = 10 hp(l). Working through the relationship above gives Rear wheel drivetrain efficiency = 1.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Rear wheel drivetrain efficiency = 1 should be roughly the size you expected from Drive type set to Rear wheel drive (RWD) and Engine horsepower = 10 hp(l).

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Power, opening in mechanical horsepowers

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Wheel horsepower calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the engine horsepower, the gearbox efficiency and the bearing efficiency — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Wheel horsepower calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns rear wheel drivetrain efficiency, derived from the engine horsepower, the gearbox efficiency and the bearing efficiency. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Wheel horsepower calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the engine horsepower, the gearbox efficiency and the bearing efficiency, which is 30 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter engine horsepower in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Engine horsepower opens in mechanical horsepowers and the chip beside it offers 21 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Rear wheel drivetrain efficiency = 1. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Wheel horsepower calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
